title: The 10 Best HVLP Paint Sprayers
subtitle: Electric HVLP paint and stain sprayers for furniture, cabinets, fences and walls, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: An HVLP sprayer atomizes paint with a high volume of low-pressure air, giving a smooth finish with less overspray than an airless sprayer. We ranked 10 best-sellers from HomeRight, Wagner, Fuji Spray, Graco and budget brands on rating, review volume and features (spraying unthinned paint, a separate turbine base, brass nozzles and flow control). Cheap handhelds need thinned paint; the turbine systems give the finest finish.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

reasons: The model number, model name and part number are all 'lqhs', and the spec table lists the sprayer's dimensions as 1 x 1 inch.

buyers_guide.a: High volume, low pressure: a turbine blows lots of air at low pressure to atomize paint. You get less overspray and bounce-back than with airless sprayers, which makes HVLP good for furniture, cabinets and trim. It's slower than airless on whole houses.

buyers_guide.q: Do I have to thin the paint?
buyers_guide.a: With most handheld HVLPs, yes, especially for latex. Use the viscosity cup to check. Wagner's FLEXiO models and Graco's EVO Plus are sold as spraying unthinned paint with the right nozzle.

Handhelds put the motor and paint in your hand, which gets heavy. Turbine systems like the Fuji Semi-PRO and Wagner Control Spray Max keep the motor on the floor with a 15 to 25 foot hose, so the gun stays light and the air stays cooler and drier.
Expect 10 to 20 minutes: run water (or the right solvent) through the gun, then take the nozzle apart and brush it. Paint left to dry in the nozzle is the most common reason sprayers stop working.

buyers_guide.q: How do I avoid runs and orange peel?
buyers_guide.a: Practice on cardboard, keep the gun 6 to 10 inches away and moving, overlap each pass by half, and spray thin coats. Orange peel usually means paint too thick or too little air.
